title: Authorization and Spend Guidance at Scale
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide guidance for authorization, procurement, expense approvals, vendor onboarding, change management, and travel. It is intended as the canonical operational reference for cross-functional teams, finance partners, and approvers. The purpose is to reduce friction, ensure consistent controls, and clarify who does what and when for commonly executed flows.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and vendors interacting with Redwood systems or spending Redwood funds.
- Covers low-touch purchases (<= $5,000), mid-tier (>$5,000 and <= $100,000), and large commitments (>$100,000), vendor onboarding, privileged access requests, emergency changes, and travel/expense reimbursements.
- Does NOT replace customer-specific legal contracts or high-security onboarding processes (see security-and-compliance vendor evidence pages).

Principles:
1) Least privilege: Grant the minimum access required for work, time-bound where possible.
2) Clear approvals: Every expenditure and access change must have a named approver with delegation recorded in the request.
3) Risk-aware procurement: Vendor classification drives required evidence and review steps.
4) Auditability: Requests must include justification, cost coding, and an attached PO or invoice when available.

Roles and ownership (short):
- Requester: Submits the access/expense/purchase or vendor request with required details.
- Approver: Team manager or delegated approver responsible for scope and budget validation.
- Finance Owner: Validates chart of accounts, budget availability, and payment terms.
- Security Reviewer: Required for vendors with data access or elevated privileges.
- Procurement Coordinator (Finance Ops): Manages vendor setup, PO issuance, and contract routing.

1) Access and permissions lifecycle:
Overview: Access requests should be submitted in the Access Request form (Confluence + internal request portal) and follow the approval matrix below. Access granting is automated where possible; manual reviews are required for privileged groups.

Approval matrix (text table):
- Routine developer access (repo/read-only): Manager approval.
- Production system access (deploy rights, admin consoles): Manager + Security Reviewer.
- Customer-data access (PII/PHI scope): Manager + Security Reviewer + Legal sign-off.

Typical request flow (numbered):
1. Requester opens ticket using the internal Access Request template and attaches justification and TTL (time-to-live).
2. Automated routing to Manager approver.
3. If role requires elevated access, route to Security for technical justification and isolation requirements.
4. Provisioning executed by identity ops; a ticket comment must include the change log, reviewer, and TTL expiration.
5. Monthly deprovisioning sweep where TTLs have expired; managers receive automated reminders 7 days prior.

Emergency access (break-glass):
- Emergency access may be granted with an expedited approval chain: Pager duty lead (or Security on-call) + Engineering manager after-the-fact review. All emergency grants must be logged and retroactively justified within 48 hours.

2) Change management (services, infra, configs):
Purpose: Reduce unplanned downtime and ensure traceability for changes affecting production or platform services.
Change types and required approvals:
- Standard change (documented, repeatable, low-risk): Pre-approved catalog; requires change ticket and owner.
- Normal change (non-repetitive, moderate risk): Requires Change Advisory Board (CAB) review and scheduled maintenance window.
- Emergency change: Rare; follows Emergency access process and post-change review.

Change request checklist (bulleted):
- Owner, rollback plan, test plan, affected services, schedule, and communications plan.
- Expected outage window (if any) and stakeholder notification list.
- Post-deployment validation steps and performance monitoring targets.

CAB cadence and responsibilities:
- CAB meets weekly; membership includes SRE lead, Platform PM, Security representative, and one service owner. CAB approves Normal changes and verifies mitigations for Standard changes when needed.

3) Data classification and data management summary:
Classification tiers (short):
- Public: No access controls required.
- Internal: Company-internal operational data.
- Confidential: Business-sensitive data; restricted to role-based groups.
- Restricted: Customer PHI/PII or regulated data; requires encryption at rest, access logging, and legal review.

Retention and deletion rules (high level):
- Default retention for internal operational logs: 90 days.
- Long-term audit logs: 7 years (Finance and Security exceptions allowed).
- Customer data retention must follow contractual obligations; operations must provide deletion confirmation within requested SLA.

Data-handling requirements for vendors:
- Vendors classified as Confidential or Restricted must sign DPA, provide SOC2 or equivalent evidence, and support secure data transfer (SFTP or private networking).

4) Procurement and expense approvals:
Approval thresholds and routing (text table):
- <= $5,000: Team manager approval; expense coding required.
- $5,000 < x <= $100,000: Manager + Finance Owner approval; Procurement Coordinator notified.
- > $100,000: Manager + Finance Director + Legal review; Procurement Coordinator leads sourcing.

Preferred purchasing flow (recommended):
1. Create a Purchase Request in the internal procurement tool with supplier details, SOW or quote, and expected deliverables.
2. Finance validates budget and issues PO where required.
3. Contracts > $25,000 require a standard procurement clause template and Legal review.
4. On invoice receipt, code against PO; Finance Ops matches 3-way (PO, Receipt, Invoice) for payment.

Expense policy highlights (travel & card spend):
- Company card charges should be reconciled weekly; receipts required for all card transactions.
- Travel per diem and class: Economy for flights < 6 hours; business for flights >= 6 hours with director approval.
- Meal per diem caps are defined in the Expense Templates page and must be itemized for reimbursement.

Example purchase request JSON (for automation):
{
  "requester": "<employee_id>",
  "department": "<cost_center>",
  "amount": "<USD>",
  "vendor": "<vendor_name>",
  "justification": "<business_reason>",
  "requested_approver": "<manager_id>"
}

5) Vendor management and onboarding:
Vendor classification (quick):
- Low-risk supplier: Office supplies, non-sensitive SaaS. Evidence: W-9, basic PO.
- Medium-risk supplier: SaaS with internal integrations. Evidence: SOC2 Type II or equivalent, contract, limited data access controls.
- High-risk supplier: Vendors handling customer data, access to production, or critical infrastructure. Evidence: DPA, SOC2, penetration test summary, insurance, and customized contractual terms.

Onboarding checklist (numbered):
1. Requester provides vendor profile and classification checklist to Procurement Coordinator.
2. Finance and Legal review contract terms and SLA; Security verifies technical controls.
3. Procurement Coordinator creates vendor record, enters payment terms, and issues PO if applicable.
4. Technical integration sandbox and least-privilege credentials created; restrict to test environment by default.
5. Go/no-go gating: Security and Finance must both sign off before production credentials are issued.

Vendor review SLA targets:
- Low-risk: 3 business days.
- Medium-risk: 7–10 business days.
- High-risk: 15–30 business days (dependent on evidence collection).

6) Travel policy and approvals (summary):
Pre-approval steps:
- Travel must be requested via the Travel Request template with purpose, attendee list, estimated cost, and preferred dates.
- Manager approval required; trips funded by sales or partnerships require Sales Director pre-approval over $10k.

Expense reconciliation timeline:
- Submit receipts and completed expense report within 10 business days of trip completion. Late submissions may be delayed for reimbursement.

7) Templates and examples (where to find and how to use):
- Access Request Template: Confluence > templates > access-request-template. Use it for TTL and justifications.
- Purchase Request Template: includes fields for budget code, contract owner, and invoice matching notes.
- Vendor Risk Assessment: fill out for any medium/high-risk supplier.
- Change Request Template: includes rollback steps and post-deploy verification checklist.

Quick reference: Approval thresholds and required reviewers:
- <= $5k: Manager.
- $5k–$100k: Manager + Finance Owner.
- > $100k: Manager + Finance Director + Legal.
- Production admin access: Manager + Security.
- Customer-data access: Manager + Security + Legal.

Operational run notes and exceptions:
- Delegation: Managers can delegate approval authority to a named delegate for up to 6 months; delegation must be recorded in the request portal.
- Exceptions: Business-critical exceptions can be escalated to the cross-functional Governance Council; all exceptions require a compensating control and retrospective review.

Change log and governance:
- This document is owned by Finance-Legal. Significant changes follow an in_review cycle with reviewers listed above. Minor clarifications may be published after internal stakeholder notification.

Contacts and escalation path:
- Procurement Coordinator (Finance Ops): finance-ops@redwood.ai
- Security intake: security-intake@redwood.ai
- Legal contracts team: legal-contracts@redwood.ai

Appendix A — Approval routing examples (CLI snippet for automation):
# Example: create purchase request via internal CLI
redwood-cli procure create --vendor "Acme AI" --amount 7500 --cost-center ENG-PLATFORM --justification "Model fine-tuning credits" --approver manager_123

Appendix B — Template checklists (copy & paste friendly):
- Purchase request: vendor, SOW/quote, budget code, approver, expected delivery date, contract owner.
- Vendor onboarding: classification, evidence checklist, contract signed, payment terms, sandbox credentials.

Related reading and references:
- See the Security & Compliance vendor evidence page for required audit artifacts.
- See the central Change Management runbook for CAB calendar and meeting notes.

End of document.
